before.title: Denso Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Impeller Swelling (Recall WRD-20)
before.description: 2018-2019 BRZs equipped with Denso-made low-pressure in-tank fuel pumps (which feed the FA20's high-pressure direct injection system). The impeller material absorbs fuel over time, swelling and deforming until the pump binds or fails. Causes loss of fuel pressure, rough running, stalling, hard starting, and potential no-start. Covered by Subaru recall WRD-20 (initial June 2020), expanded as WRG-21 in September 2021; part of the broader 165,000+ vehicle Subaru/Denso recall and class action settlement.
before.solution: Free dealer replacement of the low-pressure fuel pump assembly under recall WRD-20. Verify VIN status at subaru.com/recalls. Do not delay - failure can leave the vehicle stranded.

before.title: FA20 Rough Idle / Hunting / Stall - ECM Reflash (TSB 11-136-14R)
before.description: Early FA20-equipped BRZs exhibit rough idle, RPM hunting, shaking, and occasional stalling shortly after cold start. Often triggers CEL with cam timing codes P0017, P0018, or P0019. Caused by ECU's reaction to normal mechanical variation in the AVCS system rather than a hardware defect. Subaru issued an ECU reflash via TSB; later production cars received the updated calibration at factory.
before.solution: Subaru TSB 11-136-14R (revised 05/13/14) ECM reprogramming resolves the issue at no cost under warranty (labor op A455-288, 0.4 hr). Production fix incorporated Sept 27, 2013, so later 2014 build-dates may already have the updated calibration. No hardware replacement needed. Verify by VIN at dealer.

before.description: Instrumented testing of 2022+ BRZs shows the FA24 stock oil pan and pickup cannot maintain oil pressure during sustained right-hand cornering at >1G. Documented pressure drops from 62 psi to 28 psi at high RPM cause rod bearing damage. Multiple track/autocross engine failures reported including Blake Alvarado's autocross blowup. before.title: FA20 Engine Oil Consumption During Spirited Driving
before.description: The FA20 engine in the BRZ consumes oil at elevated rates during high-RPM driving, spirited canyon runs, and track use. The engine design with direct injection and high compression (12.5:1) combined with the oil-fed variable valve timing system means oil consumption increases significantly when the engine is frequently operated above 5,000 RPM. Consumption rates of 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles are reported by owners who drive aggressively. The narrow oil galleries in the FA20 make proper oil level maintenance critical.
before.solution: Check oil level before and after every spirited drive or track day. Carry an extra quart of 0W-20 (OEM spec) or 5W-30 (commonly used upgrade for track use). For track cars, install an oil catch can (Radium Engineering 20-0255-02 or Crawford Performance V3) to reduce oil vapor entering the intake. Consider an oil cooler for track use. Subaru considers up to 1 qt per 3,000 miles as acceptable.
symptoms: Oil level drops noticeably after spirited driving or track days
Low oil pressure warning during hard cornering (oil starvation)
Oil consumption of 1 qt per 1,000-2,000 miles with aggressive driving
Oil level normal during city/highway commuting but drops during performance driving

citations.description: FT86Club oil consumption tracking thread with data from 500+ owners

communityRecommendations.text: Install an oil catch can - it prevents oil vapor from coating the intake valves (direct injection means no fuel wash) and reduces consumption
For track use, switch to 5W-30 (Motul 8100 X-cess or Pennzoil Ultra Platinum) - provides better protection at sustained high RPM

communityRecommendations.content: High-quality synthetic oil helps reduce consumption and protect worn engines
communityRecommendations.partName: Extended Performance Full Synthetic Motor Oil

communityRecommendations.content: Premium oil filter ensures proper filtration with high-mileage engines

before.title: Second Generation Rear Differential Whine/Noise
before.description: 2022+ second-generation BRZs (and twin Toyota GR86) have reports of rear differential whine or droning noise, particularly noticeable at 30-50 mph during deceleration and light throttle. The noise comes from the ring and pinion gear mesh in the Torsen limited-slip differential. While some gear noise is normal for an LSD, affected vehicles have excessive noise audible inside the cabin. Subaru released TSB 03-73-23 addressing differential noise with fluid replacement procedure.
before.solution: Have dealer perform differential fluid replacement per TSB 03-73-23 using Subaru 75W-90 GL-5 gear oil with friction modifier (Subaru SOA427V1710). The break-in fluid is replaced with the updated fluid and an additive that reduces gear mesh noise. If noise persists after fluid change, ring and pinion inspection and possible replacement may be needed under warranty.
symptoms: Whining noise from rear of vehicle at 30-50 mph
Droning sound that varies with speed, not RPM
Noise may quiet down after differential warms up
Sound more prominent with windows up in quiet cabin

citations.description: FT86Club thread on 2nd gen rear diff whine reports

communityRecommendations.text: The dealer fluid change per TSB 03-73-23 resolves the noise for most owners - insist on this being done if you hear the whine
Some gear whine is normal for the Torsen LSD - if it doesn't bother you during normal driving, it's not hurting anything

before.title: Throwout Bearing Noise and Premature Failure
before.description: Manual transmission BRZs commonly develop throwout bearing (release bearing) noise, typically a chirping, squealing, or grinding sound when the clutch pedal is pressed or released. The noise is most apparent in cold weather and often appears between 20,000-60,000 miles. While the noise itself is mostly a nuisance, a failed throwout bearing can cause clutch disengagement problems. Subaru has not issued a recall, but the issue is well-documented across both BRZ and Toyota 86 communities. Replacement requires transmission removal.
before.solution: Replace throwout bearing (Subaru 30502AA162 or Koyo equivalent). before.title: FA20 Valve Spring Recall - Engine Stalling Risk
before.description: The FA20 engine in 2013-2016 BRZs was subject to a safety recall (WQG-66 / NHTSA 18V-845) for defective valve springs that can fracture due to insufficient hardness. A broken valve spring causes a cylinder misfire and can lead to engine stalling. In worst cases, the broken spring allows valve-to-piston contact, causing catastrophic engine damage. Subaru recalls affected VINs for free valve spring replacement. The recall also affects the Toyota 86/Scion FR-S which shares the same engine.
before.solution: Check recall status by VIN at subaru.com/owners/recalls. Recall WQG-66 (NHTSA 18V-845) covers free replacement of all intake and exhaust valve springs (16 total) at Subaru dealer. If valve-to-piston contact occurred, engine replacement is covered under the recall. Do not delay - a broken valve spring can cause catastrophic engine damage.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire code (P0301-P0304)
Engine stalling at idle or low speed
Ticking or unusual noise from engine top end
